newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms, interbank eases on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms, interbank eases on IMF news.

text.p: News that the IMF is involved in solving Thailand's battered economy helped lift gloom in the money market, pushing the baht higher and the interbank rate lower late on Monday, dealers said.
The baht edged up to 31.90-32.00 baht per dollar compared with 32.100-32.200 early in the local market and 31.550-31.850 in the offshore market from 31.800-32.050 earlier in the day.
"There was more dollar buying today than in the past week. It could be from exporters or portfolio investors who need baht to invest in the stock market,' said a dealer at a US bank.
The SET index surged 5.27 percent higher to close at 680.67 on Monday as market optimism grew on possibilities that Thailand may take some sort of financial assistance from the IMF.

Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya said on Monday that he was meeting a five-man IMF team in Bangkok for a week to seek advice on how Thailand could resolve economic crisis, but said Thailand needed to study if IMF borrowings were necessary.

Separately, however, central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond told reporters that Thai premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh and Thanong had agreed in principle since July 22 to tap loans from IMF. He had no details on what sort of loans.

"Dollar buying on commercial demand continued but it's the increase in selling of the unit that propped up the baht. The volume also picked up to between $700-$1.0 billion from around an average of $400 million in the past week," said another dealer at an European bank here.
The overnight interbank rate was quoted around 14-16 percent late from 14.00-17.00 early on increased liquidity, and it is expected to drop further.
"Noticeable foreign inflows entered the market through the swap market and the stock market," said a dealer at a major foreign bank.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium softened to around 12/17 satangs per dollar from 20-30 satangs early, dealer said.
